key_insight: RubriQ turns quantum circuit synthesis into an LLM code-generation problem and uses rubric-guided GRPO to optimize for correctness, hardware compatibility, and T-gate efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers an HPC-scalable path to produce fault-tolerant, hardware-ready quantum circuits automatically, reducing manual synthesis effort for near-term and fault-tolerant quantum workflows.
method: LLM generates candidate quantum circuits as code.
A programmatic rubric scores T-gate reduction, topology compliance, and unitary fidelity.
CUDA-Q simulation and DeepSpeed ZeRO2 enable high-throughput RL training on multinode A100 clusters.
evidence_signal: In benchmark evaluations, RubriQ achieved a mean 3.31x T-gate compression, converged 2-3x faster than sparse-reward RL baselines, and kept hardware-constraint violations below 1%.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate simulation and rubric design, so performance may be sensitive to simulator fidelity, reward specification, and transfer from simulated to real hardware.
paper_title: RubriQ: Rubric-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization for Constraint-Aware Quantum Circuit Synthesis
